name: Four-leg desk or table
tagline: A top, four legs, and a crossbar. The easiest piece of furniture there is, if you tighten in the right order.
peopleNote: One person, two if the top is glass or very large.

tools.why: Faster for the many small screws in a leg plate.

tools.n: A bubble level or the level app on your phone
tools.why: Checking the top before you load it with a monitor.

before: Work with the top upside down on the flattened box. You will do nine tenths of the job this way.
Keep screws in their bags. A desk kit often has three screw lengths and the long one through a thin top goes straight out the other side.
Decide which way the desk will face now, so the cable notch and the modesty panel end up at the back.
safety: Never put weight on a desk whose bolts are only finger-tight.
Glass tops: lift with two people, never by one edge, and never set a glass edge down on a hard floor.

steps.title: Top upside down, good face protected
steps.say: Lay the desktop upside down on the flattened cardboard. Working this way means gravity is holding the legs in place instead of fighting you.
do: Good face down, onto cardboard or a blanket
Pre-drilled holes facing up at you
Sweep the floor first — one bit of grit scratches a whole top

steps.title: Work out front, back, left and right
steps.say: Find the back edge. It is usually the one with a cable notch, a rougher finish, or extra bracket holes. Mark it so you cannot forget.
do: Look for a cable cut-out or grommet hole: that is the back
Compare the two long edges for finish quality
Put a sticky note on the back edge
steps.watch: A desk assembled front-to-back has its cable notch against the wall and all its bracket screws visible. Thirty seconds now.

steps.title: Check the screws go in the right holes
steps.say: Hold each screw next to the thickness of the top. If a screw is longer than the top is thick, it does not belong in the top.
do: Short fat screws: into the top
Long bolts: through the legs into a threaded insert
Compare lengths side by side against the manual's picture
steps.watch: A too-long screw driven into a desktop punches a visible dimple or a hole right through the finished surface. This is permanent.

steps.title: Attach the legs, finger-tight
steps.say: Put each leg or leg plate on its holes and start every screw before tightening any. Four legs, all loose.
do: Line the plate up square with the edges of the top
Start all screws by hand
Legs should point straight up, not splayed
steps.tip: Legs often have a top and bottom. The end with the adjustable foot goes to the floor.

steps.title: Fit the crossbar or stretcher
steps.say: The bar between the legs is not decoration. It is the thing that stops the desk from racking side to side. Bolt it in while everything is still loose.
do: Bolt both ends finger-tight
If there are two bars, fit both
Check it is not upside down — bolt holes usually only match one way
steps.watch: Skipping the crossbar because it looked optional is the number one cause of a wobbly desk.

steps.title: Tighten in a cross pattern, twice
steps.say: Tighten opposite corners rather than going round in order, like a car wheel. Then do a second lap. This pulls the desk into square by itself.
do: Front-left, then back-right, then front-right, then back-left
Crossbar last
Second full lap
steps.tip: Firm, then stop. Chipboard and MDF strip easily, and a stripped leg plate is a desk that never stops wobbling.

steps.title: Flip it over, carefully
steps.say: Lift it rather than rolling it over on a leg. Legs levered sideways is exactly how leg plates get bent and screws get stripped.
do: Lift from the top itself, not the legs
Two people if it is large or glass
Set it down on all four feet at once
steps.watch: Never flip a desk by pushing it over onto one pair of legs. That load goes straight into the screw threads.

steps.title: Level it and kill the wobble
steps.say: Push each corner. If it rocks, turn the adjustable foot on the leg that lifts off the floor until all four sit down. Then check the top is level.
do: Press each corner in turn to find the short leg
Screw that foot out until the rock stops
Lay a level on the top, side to side and front to back
steps.tip: If the legs have no adjustable feet, a folded index card or a stick-on felt pad under the short leg works permanently and silently.

steps.title: Run the cables before you load it up
steps.say: Thread your power strip and cables now, while the desk is empty and light enough to move. Afterwards it is a wrestling match.
do: Mount the power strip to the underside with its screw holes or velcro
Feed cables through the notch or grommet
Use a few cable ties along the crossbar
steps.tip: Leave each cable a little slack where it reaches the monitor so you can still tilt and swivel.

fixes.q: The desk wobbles however much I tighten it
fixes.a: Three usual causes: the crossbar is missing or loose, the floor is uneven and the feet need adjusting, or a leg plate screw is stripped. Check in that order.

fixes.q: A screw went through the top
fixes.a: It was the wrong length. Back it out, fill the hole with a wax touch-up stick or colored filler, and use the correct short screw. Compare lengths before driving the rest.

fixes.q: A leg plate screw spins and will not bite
fixes.a: Stripped hole. Push a wooden toothpick or two with a drop of wood glue into the hole, let it set, then re-drive. Or move to a fresh hole a half inch away if the plate allows.

fixes.q: The desk is not level even though it does not rock
fixes.a: Rock and level are different problems. Use a level on the top and adjust the feet on the low side until the bubble centers.

fixes.q: The cable notch ended up facing the room
fixes.a: The top is on back-to-front. Unscrew the legs, rotate the top, re-screw. Twenty minutes and no harm done — the holes are symmetrical on nearly every desk.
